newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees no need for curbs on foreign brewers.
newsitem.headline: China sees no need for curbs on foreign brewers.

text.p: A Chinese investment official said on Wednesday Beijing had concluded there was no need to block further investment by foreign brewers in the domestic market.
"The debate has been put to rest," said Sun Huaiyu, director of the foreign investment office of the central city of Wuhan.

Sun said he had been advised by senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation that new projects or the expansion of existing ones were acceptable if they contributed to economic growth or strengthened China's technical capacity.
Sun told an investment seminar that officials normally evaluated investment plans for their possible impact on domestic companies and for possible loss of state assets.
But he said officials in Beijing had concluded that the foreign share of the beer market was still small and should not be restricted if it contributed to economic development.
"There are more benefits than drawbacks" to foreign investment in the sector, Sun said.
Many domestic companies in many industries, including brewing, have come under pressure from foreign competitors as China opens its markets.
Industry officials said brewing was one area where there was pressure for protection of domestic producers.
An official of Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc told the seminar that the company was waiting for approval for an expansion plan that would double capacity at its Wuhan brewery. She gave no further details.
